comparison: Perfect agreement on precursor relationships (C7, C40-C42, C59). Both evaluations find the model comparison approach and LOO-IC methodology compelling and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative support while peer reviewers highlight the novelty of modeling different recruitment modes.

Perfect agreement on main conclusions (C46-C47, C60). Both evaluations strongly support these synthesis claims. OpenEval notes convergence of multiple analytical approaches, while peer reviewers describe it as 'a fundamental advance' with 'compelling' evidence.

Perfect agreement on steady-state assumption (C23, C50). Both evaluations support the empirical justification based on lack of age-related changes. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the rigorous analysis without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on key observation from Cd4-FR experiments (C24-C25). Both evaluations support this fundamental observation of slow decline in mTom+ cells. OpenEval emphasizes its importance for subsequent modeling, peer reviewers accept it as strong evidence.

Disagreement on Ki67 convergence kinetics (C26-C27, C38-C39). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED with consistency to prior literature, but peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY with editor noting 'open questions on the interpretation of the Ki67-based fate mapping remain.'

Agreement on independent validation approach (C43-C45). Both evaluations support the Ki67-based validation despite editor's note about 'open questions' on Ki67 interpretation. The agreement between methods is seen as strengthening conclusions by both evaluations.

Strong agreement on skin TRM kinetic parameters (C2-C4, C28, C30, C32-C33, C36). OpenEval emphasizes convergence with Ki67 validation, peer reviewers describe evidence as 'compelling' and 'rigorous' with no concerns raised. Peer review R1 also includes LP TRM claims that OpenEval separates into R2.

Strong agreement on LP TRM kinetic parameters (C5-C6, C29, C34-C35, C37). OpenEval separates LP TRM analysis from skin TRM, while peer reviewers group all kinetic parameters together in R1. Both find the tissue-specific differences well-supported.

Agreement on genetic reporter systems (C62-C65). OpenEval emphasizes established characterization in prior literature, peer reviewers describe mouse strains as 'elegant' and 'powerful.' OpenEval R10 includes C62-C65, peer R9 also includes C66.

Agreement on tissue localization validation (C66). OpenEval supports the discrimination between tissue-resident and circulating cells, peer reviewers accept technical validity. OpenEval separates C66 into R11, while peer reviewers group it with reporter systems in R9.

Difference in evaluation stringency for speculation (C48). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting it is explicitly speculative without direct evidence, while peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting appropriately framed interpretations. Peer R8 groups multiple speculative claims together.

Difference in evaluation stringency for speculation (C61). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting conditional nature and lack of direct evidence linking kinetics to immunity duration, while peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED as part of accepted interpretive framework.

Agreement on limitations and alternative scenarios (C52-C53 overlap). OpenEval groups broader set of limitation claims (C49, C52-C53, C56-C58) as SUPPORTED, peer reviewers group speculative statements (C48, C52-C53, C61) as SUPPORTED, both accepting appropriate scientific caution.
OpenEval evaluates comparison to published rates (C31) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citation context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific comparison claim.

OpenEval evaluates mathematical model properties and predictions (C51, C54-C55) as SUPPORTED with note that experimental validation would strengthen support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific model-based inferences.
OpenEval evaluates literature context and background claims (C1, C9-C19, C67-C72) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
